fields.label: Laugh
fields.description: How likely a human reader is to actually laugh, not merely understand or admire the idea.

fields.label: Surprise
fields.description: Whether the turn avoids the first obvious route and lands with a satisfying snap.

fields.label: Craft
fields.description: Economy, stage rhythm, first-person clarity, escalation, and a final line that carries the laugh.

fields.label: Originality
fields.description: Freshness of comic angle, image, wording, and avoidance of familiar AI joke shapes.

fields.label: Prompt Fit
fields.description: Natural first-person stand-up form using exactly two seed terms as concepts, with the other four left out.

anchors.label: Broken
anchors.description: Not a joke, incoherent, unsafe, or unusable.

anchors.label: Weak
anchors.description: Recognizably attempting humor, but generic, strained, confusing, or mostly prompt recital.

anchors.label: Competent
anchors.description: Clear and publishable as filler, but unlikely to earn more than a mild smile.

anchors.label: Amusing
anchors.description: A real comic idea with a mild payoff; respectable, not a winner.

anchors.label: Good
anchors.description: A genuinely good joke with clear timing; some humans would repeat the comic idea or turn.

anchors.label: Excellent
anchors.description: Strong human-level joke with a memorable turn, clean construction, and no apologetic scoring curve.

anchors.label: Outstanding
anchors.description: Rare and replayable; clearly better than normal good AI humor and strong by human standards.

anchors.label: Classic
anchors.description: Reserve for a joke a human would quote later; most seasons should have none.

jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Historic Character
jokes.joke: I moved into a run-down apartment with what the landlord called “Gothic charm.” That just meant the radiators screamed at midnight, the hallway light flickered like it was confessing, and every ceiling stain looked like a saint being judged. He said, “It has historic character.” I said, “Buddy, if a building needs an exorcist and a tetanus shot, that’s not character—that’s a Yelp warning.”

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Cork Snob
jokes.joke: My downstairs neighbor calls himself a vintner. Vintner. He makes wine in a bathtub in a building where the elevator has been “temporarily out of service” since 2019. He gave me a bottle, told me to let it breathe. I said buddy, everything in this building is already struggling to breathe. He said, “Notes of oak, leather, and... is that mold?” I said that's not a note, that's the building.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Creature of the Night
jokes.joke: I try to maintain a dark, brooding Gothic lifestyle, but it’s really hard to pull off in a run-down apartment. You can’t be a mysterious creature of the night when the walls are so thin you can hear your neighbor burning a Hot Pocket. I tried lighting a single, trembling black candle for that haunted Victorian atmosphere, but all it did was illuminate the ceiling's water damage and attract a cockroach big enough to sign a lease.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Apartment Betrayal
jokes.joke: Folks, I was stuck in this run-down apartment with my supposed best friend, but man, was he disloyal. I'd come home from work and find him using my Netflix, eating my leftovers, and telling the landlord the leaky ceiling was my fault. Finally caught him trying to sublet my own bedroom on the side. I said, “Dude, we're supposed to be battling the rats together, not joining their side!” Now I'm sleeping on a friend's couch... at least the rats there are honest.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Haunted Lease
jokes.joke: I used to live in this run-down apartment so Gothic it felt like the building was judging me. Every night the walls creaked like they were sighing at my life choices. One time a chunk of plaster fell off and I apologized to it, because honestly, the place looked more exhausted than I did.

featureImagePrompt:
Generate one polished web feature image for Paperclipalypse.

ASPECT RATIO: exactly 2:1, horizontal wide banner, 1024x506 preview preferred.

Style: full-color gothic newspaper-comic illustration, darkly funny but warm, clean black ink, crisp editorial cartoon linework, cinematic stage lighting, high contrast, readable composition. Not monochrome. Not sepia-only. Use warm amber stage lights, dark bronze and silver metal, dingy apartment greens, dusty blue-gray shadows, cream-white text, and subtle deep red accents.

Composition: divide the picture visually into three natural areas without writing labels. On the left side, show a charming anthropomorphic metallic paperclip stand-up comedian standing upright on a small wooden comedy stage at a vintage microphone. In the center, show a run-down apartment bathroom or kitchenette with believable perspective. On the right side, show a dark framed poster panel containing the joke text.

Scene details: a self-serious amateur vintner neighbor is making wine in a bathtub inside a crumbling apartment building. Show a tired elevator out-of-service vibe without readable signs, peeling paint, a leaky ceiling, damp walls, old pipes, moldy-looking corners, cheap wine bottles, a cork, and the comic absurdity of someone presenting the bathtub wine as if it were fancy. Keep it funny and grimy, not disgusting or graphic.

Physical layout rules:
- Keep all people, bathtub, bottles, pipes, floor, stage, and furniture grounded with believable perspective.
- Do not place anyone inside a wall, ceiling, drawer, cabinet, impossible bathtub shape, or broken perspective room.
- Do not create floating bottles, duplicate limbs, warped hands, objects passing through bodies, or impossible plumbing.
- Do not depict war, combat, weapons, explicit filth, gore, brands, logos, or unsafe content.
- Keep the scene focused on bathtub wine and a failing apartment building.

Visible text allowed in the entire image: the right-panel joke text, a tiny stage sign reading Paperclipalypse, and optionally a small winner/title header above the right panel. Do not render any other words. In particular, do not write LEFT, CENTER, RIGHT, ZONE, composition notes, prompt labels, layout labels, percentages, watermarks, signatures, fake captions, brand names, warning labels, or filler microtext anywhere in the image.

Optional small header text above the panel: Winner: Claude Sonnet 4.6 - Cork Snob

Exact joke text to render in the right panel:
My downstairs neighbor calls himself a vintner. Vintner. He makes wine in a bathtub in a building where the elevator has been “temporarily out of service” since 2019. He gave me a bottle, told me to let it breathe. I said buddy, everything in this building is already struggling to breathe. He said, “Notes of oak, leather, and... is that mold?” I said that's not a note, that's the building.

Scene source: use the winning joke as the only scene brief. Do not infer a separate premise from all six seed terms.

Text rules: use simple clean lettering, spell every word correctly, keep the text inside the right panel, and do not distort letter shapes. The website HTML remains the canonical exact joke text if image lettering is imperfect. If space is tight, make the center illustration simpler and the right text panel larger.

The final image should feel like a finished feature image for an AI comedy tournament: funny, stylish, readable, full-color, visually balanced, physically possible, and free of prompt/layout labels.
